AC Gas Filling Cost – R32 vs R410A Explained (2026 Guide)

What AC gas filling really costs, how R32 and R410A differ, what pushes the price up, and how to avoid paying for gas that leaks out again.

Written by BOBBY AC Repair & Home Appliance ServicesPublished 24 Nov 2026Updated 24 Nov 2026

This article is currently available in English.

In this article

  • Typical AC gas filling charges in India (2026)
  • R32 vs R410A: what is the difference?
  • Never mix gases
  • What affects the price
  • Signs your AC really needs gas
  • Gas filling in inverter ACs
  • How to avoid overpaying
  • The honest way to fill AC gas

Quick answer: in 2026, AC gas filling for a typical home split AC in India usually costs about ₹2,000–₹3,500, and can reach ₹4,500 in some cities or for larger units. In Narasaraopet, BOBBY's estimate range is ₹2,000–₹3,500 per AC, including a leak check. R32 is now the most common gas in new Indian ACs; R410A is found in many older and some commercial units. The bigger cost question is not the gas type but whether a leak is repaired first.

Typical AC gas filling charges in India (2026)

AC typeCommon gasTypical range
Split AC, 1–1.5 tonR32 / R410A₹2,000 – ₹3,500
Split AC, 2 tonR32 / R410A₹2,500 – ₹4,500
Window AC (older)R22 / R32₹1,800 – ₹3,000
Leak repair (brazing / flare joint)–Extra, quoted after inspection

These are market ranges reported by large national service platforms; local prices vary with the gas price, how much refrigerant is needed and the work involved. For your own AC in Narasaraopet, see a quick estimate here or read our AC gas filling service page.

R32 vs R410A: what is the difference?

R32R410AR22 (old)
Global warming potential (GWP)675about 2,088about 1,810
Ozone depletionZeroZeroDepletes ozone (being phased out)
CompositionSingle gasBlend of two gasesSingle gas
Top-upCan be topped up on siteUsually recover and recharge fullyOld units only
Where you find itMost new inverter split ACsOlder split and some commercial ACsOlder window/split ACs

R32 has roughly one-third the global warming impact of R410A, which is why most manufacturers have moved to it. Because R32 is a single-component gas, it can be topped up without changing its composition; R410A is a blend, so a careful technician usually recovers it and recharges by weight. Both R32 and R410A run at high pressure, so the right gauges and tools matter.

Never mix gases

Your AC is designed for one refrigerant; it is printed on the outdoor unit's rating sticker. Filling R32 into an R410A system (or the reverse) damages performance and can harm the compressor. A genuine technician always reads the sticker first.

What affects the price

  • How much gas is needed: a small top-up costs less than a full recharge after a big leak.
  • Leak repair: finding and brazing or re-flaring the leak adds cost but saves you a repeat refill.
  • Vacuuming: after a leak or repair, the system should be vacuumed to remove air and moisture before charging.
  • Pipe length and tonnage: bigger ACs and long pipe runs hold more refrigerant.
  • Inverter vs non-inverter: not usually a big price difference for gas itself.

Signs your AC really needs gas

  • Cooling has dropped gradually over weeks, not suddenly.
  • Ice or frost on the thinner copper pipe or the indoor coil.
  • The outdoor unit runs, but the large pipe is not cold to touch.
  • Oily marks at pipe joints or valves (refrigerant carries oil).
  • A hissing sound near the joints.

If cooling stopped suddenly, or the outdoor fan is not running, the problem is more likely electrical (capacitor, contactor, PCB) than gas.

Gas filling in inverter ACs

Most inverter ACs in India use R32. The process is the same (leak check, repair, vacuum, charge by weight to the nameplate figure), but inverter systems are sensitive to overcharging, so "adding a little extra" is a mistake. A correct charge matters for efficiency and compressor life.

How to avoid overpaying

  • Ask for the pressure reading before and after.
  • Ask where the leak was and how it was fixed.
  • Confirm the gas type matches the outdoor unit sticker.
  • Get the price confirmed before the work starts.

The honest way to fill AC gas

  1. Check cooling, airflow and filters: many "gas problems" are actually dirty coils.
  2. Measure the pressure against the gas type on the sticker.
  3. If low, find the leak (joints, valves, coils) and repair it.
  4. Vacuum the system.
  5. Charge the correct gas to the manufacturer's standard.
  6. Test cooling and pressures before leaving.

This is exactly how BOBBY handles gas filling in Narasaraopet. If you are told your AC "needs gas every year", there is a leak; see when AC gas filling is really required.

Frequently asked questions

How much does AC gas filling cost in Narasaraopet?

BOBBY's estimate range is ₹2,000–₹3,500 per AC, including a leak check. Any leak repair is quoted after inspection, before work starts.

Is R32 better than R410A?

R32 has about one-third of the global warming potential of R410A, zero ozone impact and is easier to top up, which is why most new ACs use it. Your AC must always be filled with the gas it was designed for.

Can R32 be filled in an R410A AC?

No. Never mix or switch refrigerants. Use only the gas printed on the outdoor unit sticker.

How long does AC gas filling last?

In a leak-free AC, many years. If gas is needed again within months, the leak was not found and repaired.
